items.question: How does Alice end up in Wonderland?
items.expected: She follows the White Rabbit (who has a watch and waistcoat) and falls down the rabbit-hole.
items.answer: Alice runs across the field after the Rabbit after seeing it take a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and she is just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge [chunk 2]. In another moment, she goes down the rabbit-hole after it without considering how she will get out again [chunk 2, chunk 3]. The rabbit-hole goes straight on like a tunnel and then dips suddenly down, causing her to fall down a very deep well [chunk 3] until she comes down upon a heap of sticks and dry leaves [chunk 8].
items.reason: The actual answer correctly captures that Alice follows the White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole, providing even more accurate details from the book.

items.question: Why does Alice start crying in the hall?
items.expected: After eating the cake she grows to over nine feet tall, so she can't get through the little door into the garden; her tears make a pool.
items.answer: Alice starts crying in the hall because she forgets the little golden key when she gets to the door, goes back to the table for it, but finds she cannot possibly reach it [chunk 15]. Later, after growing more than nine feet high and trying to look through into the garden with one eye, she realizes getting through is hopeless and sits down to cry again [chunk 20].
